questions.question: A 'Stafne bone cavity' is a normal anatomical variant of the mandible caused by the presence or pressure from which structure?
questions.detail: A Stafne bone cavity is a depression in the mandible created by the submandibular gland.

questions.question: Where is a Stafne bone cavity typically located on the mandible?
choices: At the inner surface of the angle of the mandible, below the inferior alveolar canal
On the lateral surface of the ramus
questions.detail: It is typically found on the inner surface of the angle of the mandible.

questions.question: A 'radicular cyst' is an inflammatory odontogenic cyst that characteristically develops at which location?
questions.detail: Radicular cysts are associated with the apex of a non-vital tooth.

questions.question: Which type of odontogenic cyst is classically associated with the crown of an unerupted tooth, such as a third molar?
questions.detail: A dentigerous cyst is characterized by its association with the crown of an unerupted tooth.

questions.question: An Odontogenic Keratocyst (OKC) is unique among jaw lesions because it typically:
choices: Grows along the length of the marrow space with minimal expansion
Is always associated with a non-vital tooth
questions.detail: Unlike many other cysts, an OKC tends to grow along the marrow space with minimal cortical expansion.

questions.question: In an adult, a 'soap-bubble' multilocular expansile appearance in the mandible is the classic radiologic presentation of:
questions.detail: Ameloblastoma is well known for its multi-loculated, 'soap-bubble' expansile appearance in the mandible.

questions.question: Which anatomical structure is involved in all three types of Le Fort fracture patterns?
questions.detail: Involvement of the pterygoid plates is the common denominator for all Le Fort fracture patterns.

questions.question: A 'Le Fort II' fracture is also commonly referred to as a:
questions.detail: The Le Fort II fracture pattern is also known as a pyramidal fracture.

questions.question: A Zygomaticomaxillary Complex (ZMC) fracture involves the dissociation of the zygoma from which three bones?
questions.detail: A ZMC fracture dissociates the zygoma from the frontal, maxillary, and temporal bones.

questions.question: Mandibular fractures frequently occur in more than one location because the mandible structurally behaves like a:
questions.detail: The mandible acts as a rigid ring; thus, a break in one part often results in a second fracture elsewhere.

questions.question: Which plane of injury is associated with a 'Le Fort III' (craniofacial dissociation) fracture?
choices: Across the nose and inferior orbital rims
Through the zygomatic arches and superior orbital fissures
questions.detail: Le Fort III fractures involve the zygomatic arches and superior orbital fissures, effectively separating the face from the cranium.

questions.question: Where is a 'torus palatinus'—a common benign bony exostosis—located?
questions.detail: Torus palatinus is a benign bony growth found at the midline of the hard palate.

questions.question: A Nasopalatine Duct Cyst (Incisive Canal Cyst) is characteristically found in the:
questions.detail: This cyst is located in the midline of the anterior maxilla.

questions.question: The imaging appearance of an Odontogenic Myxoma is often similar to an ameloblastoma but may specifically show:
questions.detail: Odontogenic Myxomas are noted for having 'tennis racket' or straight-line internal septations on imaging.

questions.question: Gorlin syndrome (Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome) is characteristically associated with the development of multiple:
questions.detail: Multiple Odontogenic Keratocysts are a hallmark feature of Gorlin syndrome.
